items.title: Can AI Invent or Just Help Scientists Work Faster? with Richard Socher - #783
items.summary: AI can help scientists write code, analyze data, and draft papers. But can it generate the ideas that lead to new discoveries? Richard Socher, former chief scientist at Salesforce, founder of You.com, and co-founder of Recursive, joins us to explore the move from AI assisting researchers to AI conducting research. Starting with AI improving AI, we examine what it takes to propose ideas, run experiments, and validate results, and how those capabilities could eventually accelerate discovery across biology, chemistry, and physics. The conversation covers Recursive’s reported results in model training and GPU kernel optimization, why fast verification matters, and how reward hacking complicates the search for real improvements. We also discuss the data and experimental infrastructure needed for broader scientific discovery, whether commercial incentives can keep increasingly capable systems aligned, and Richard’s vision for a “Eureka machine.” 🗒️ Full show notes: ⁠https://twimlai.com/go/783.
items.podcastDescription: Ricerca, machine learning e applicazioni raccontati da ricercatori e professionisti.

items.title: AI is destroying my CS degree
items.summary: My comment on AI is destroying my CS degree — Hacker News. I don't envy educators right now. AI clearly means you need to change how you teach and evaluate students. We are only a few years in though, and it's still extremely unclear what effective teaching with these tools looks like. The worst part is that the evaluation loop is measured in multiple years! If you start trying some new education mechanism today you won't get a robust idea of how well it works until your current cohort graduate in 3-6 years time. items.title: Palette: teaching a small model to build decks in your design language
Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too
items.summary: Yesterday's hot paper was Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights by Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab. The paper (OK, the authors classify is as a "blog post", but it's paper-shaped) found that frontier models, in particular GPT-6 Astra, can both interpret and modify the raw weights of a machine learning model - literally a text description of the model containing a bunch of floating point numbers. I've been playing with one of the examples from the paper and I'm delighted to share that Qwen 3.8 27B running on my laptop can do this as well! Weight-Space Programming Here's the highlight from their abstract, describing impressive capabilities for GPT-6 Astra and coining the term Weight-Space Programming for when LLMs analyze and modify model weights: Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do . And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps. Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights . With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and generalizes out of the box to instruction following, raising IFEval by 3x. All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops. It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly. We call this Weight-Space Programming . items.summary: Release: llm 0.37 There's a lot of stuff in this new release of my LLM CLI tool and Python library, representing around two months of accumulated features and fixes. I added gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.1-terra , plus a new llm openai endpoint add command to make it easier to configure additional models that use OpenAI-compatible endpoints. I switched the default model (if you have not set your own default) to gpt-6-luna - half the price of the previous default, gpt-5.6-luna . LLM's support for embeddings now accepts that different binary content may have different content-type - necessary for models like Gemini Embedding 2 , which can embed text, audio, images, and video. A lot of open source maintainers complain about a flood of AI-assisted PRs. LLM is my project that has been most affected by this and, to be honest, I'm not finding it to be a problem. That's mainly because I have Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra help me with triage to spot the most useful fixes! This release includes fixes from 12 authors - almost all AI-assisted - and the burden of reviewing them wasn't nearly as great as I expected. I really see them as bug reports with attached examples - sometimes I land them, sometimes I implement my own fix. So thanks to 0d00ciallo0721 , ac1982 , Allen Flux , Bian Yuhan , Bishop Kammeraad , Chen Yufeiyang , Christopher Krah , Ethan Stoner , Jiachen Xie , Olamide Faniyan , Sharat Chandra Sai Boddu , nosmile99 for helping out with (or spending tokens on) this release! it.why_it_matters: Affrontare la privacy e la riservatezza dei dati è una delle sfide cruciali nello sviluppo di strumenti di intelligenza artificiale per settori regolamentati come quello legale.
it.extended_analysis:
Lo sviluppo di agenti autonomi in contesti ad alta sensibilità informativa richiede soluzioni architetturali innovative per garantire la totale riservatezza. Poiché i dati appartengono ai clienti dello studio legale, i progettisti devono trovare metodi rigorosi per verificare le prestazioni senza violare il segreto professionale o accedere ai contenuti operativi.

L'intervista con Jacob Lauritzen offre uno sguardo approfondito sulle metodologie ingegneristiche adottate da una delle aziende a maggiore crescita nel settore, evidenziando il bilanciamento tra automazione avanzata e rigidi vincoli di sicurezza dei dati.
it.context: Il settore legale richiede standard di confidenzialità estremamente elevati, rendendo complessa l'adozione di soluzioni basate su modelli linguistici e agenti autonomi.
key_takeaways: La gestione della riservatezza dei dati dei clienti nello sviluppo di agenti legali.
Le strategie di testing e sviluppo adottate in assenza di visibilità diretta sui dati.

it.title: Scaling Git in casa OpenAI: nasce Pando

it.why_it_matters: L'evoluzione degli strumenti di supporto è cruciale per reggere i carichi di lavoro e la scala dello sviluppo guidato dall'intelligenza artificiale.

Man mano che l'uso di strumenti di codifica basati sull'intelligenza artificiale come Codex accelera la produzione di codice, i sistemi di controllo di versione tradizionali possono incontrare limiti di scala. Per affrontare questa sfida, OpenAI ha sviluppato Pando, un backend compatibile con Git.

Questo progetto illustra come le infrastrutture interne debbano evolversi parallelamente ai modelli avanzati per supportare flussi di lavoro ingegneristici massicci. Gli sviluppatori dovranno monitorare l'evoluzione di Pando per capire se soluzioni simili verranno adottate più ampiamente.

items.title: The U.S. Census Bureau and “Super Intelligence”
items.summary: I was reminded today of AI Adoption Rate Trending Down for Large Companies , a chart produced by Apollo Global Management in September 2025, which appeared to show a slowdown in U.S. corporate AI adoption based on numbers collected by the U.S. Census Bureau. At the time I used that chart to demonstrate GPT-5 data analysis , and then to experiment with Claude's new Code Interpreter . I decided to try running those numbers again to see what had changed over the past year, and in doing so learned that the Bureau has fallen foul of Executive Order 14434 , aka the asinine Super Intelligence one. First, the updated chart Every two weeks the U.S. Census Bureau runs a survey called the Business Trends and Outlook Survey (aka BTOS). Each time it goes to 200,000 businesses out of 1.2 million total - the surveyed group (a "panel") cycles such that an individual business only completes the survey every twelve weeks. The latest data is published on alternating Thursdays at 10am. I used the most recent numbers (published October 22, 2026) to create a new version ( GPT-6 Astra Extra High transcript ) of the AI adoption chart, updated to reflect both the last twelve months and a change that was made to the survey question sent out by the Bureau: Here's a link to the larger image . For comparison, here's that AI adoption chart from last year (my GPT-5 version): In September 2025 the largest (250+ employees) companies answered "yes" around 12% of the time to the question about whether they used AI in "producing goods or services". Under the new "any business function" wording, by February 2026, those same large companies answered "yes" around 30% of the time, and by October 2026 that had increased to around 40%. items.title: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file
items.summary: I've been getting the occasional confusing Python dependency error since switching over to Python 3.15 and the rule I'm having to remember is: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file Most of my projects are libraries which don't include a uv.lock file, since it's rude for a library dependency to lock versions for anything else that uses it. Running uv run pytest etc tends to leave uv.lock files lying around, which are listed in .gitignore and so do not get committed to my repositories. But... sometimes that uv.lock pins a version of a dependency that doesn't yet have a Python 3.15 wheel. An example from earlier today: error: Failed to build `watchfiles==1.1.1` cause: Call to `maturin.build_wheel` failed error: the configured Python interpreter version (3.15) is newer than PyO3's maximum supported version (3.14) Deleting that file and running uv run pytest again usually fixes the problem. Tags: uv , til , python

items.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
items.summary: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts Parameter Labs describe an exploit they found against ChatGPT's implementation of the artifacts pattern (OpenAI used to call this "Canvas" but it looks like the latest revision is called HTML previews ), where interactive custom HTML apps are displayed in a sandboxed iframe. It's important that HTML in these stays tightly sandboxed to avoid untrusted code interacting with OpenAI APIs and accessing private data. Parameter found quite a complex attack chain. OpenAI use the MathLive JavaScript library as part of their graph support, and that library includes its own virtual keyboard , which can be triggered in the parent page via postMessage() from the sandboxed iframe. That message receiving code uses innerHTML , so anything that sends a message can add custom HTML to the parent - and there was no mechanism to prevent other sandboxed frames, including HTML preview frames, from calling that method. This meant untrusted code in an iframe could insert HTML, and while innerHTML doesn't directly execute script elements it could be used to inject a new iframe without sandbox restrictions. OpenAI’s CSP rules blocked inline scripts entirely, and only allowed script loading from a handful of domains, but one of those was YouTube - and the YouTube oEmbed endpoint could be used to reflect JavaScript back in a way that executed it. Once the attack had JavaScript execution on ChatGPT, it was trivial to fetch private user data from APIs and exfiltrate it via an image reference. The end result: you could create a ChatGPT share URL which, when visited by another signed-in user, could exfiltrate their private data or take actions on their behalf. items.title: dbreunig/nesformer
items.summary: dbreunig/nesformer Inspired by qwenputer by Divyansh Agrawal, Drew Breunig baked a working emulator for a Nintendo Entertainment System 6502 CPU into the weights of Qwen3.5-4B. You can now play NES ROMs such as Super Mario Bros (very slowly) running inside Qwen! In a comment on Hacker News Drew reveals the Opus 5.5 prompts he used to build this system: Read this article and any relevant source code: https://divagr.com/blog/qwenputer. Then explore if you could emulate the chip and ram in a Nintendo Entertainment System (as people do today with FPGAs in MISTRs) using this technique. If so, what size model would you have to build and if you could use smaller faster ones, could you get it to be at the standard clockspeed. Followed by: I think we should build it! Just for fun. It's okay if it's not fast. We want to be able to have the weights, and a cli to run them that we can point at a ROM. Apparently Opus found and then used this collection of conformance tests for the NES CPU released 15 years ago by Christopher Pow. Via Hacker News Tags: games , ai , generative-ai , llms , drew-breunig , qwen , conformance-suites

it.title: Preferenze di addestramento IA: OpenAI adotta un segnale robots.txt condiviso
it.summary: OpenAI ha annunciato che onorerà un segnale robots.txt condiviso. Questa iniziativa punta ad agevolare i gestori dei siti web nel comunicare le proprie preferenze in merito all'addestramento dell'intelligenza artificiale ai provider partecipanti.
it.why_it_matters: La mossa offre un metodo strutturato per i proprietari di siti web per esprimere le preferenze sull'utilizzo dei propri dati nell'addestramento IA, coinvolgendo provider partecipanti tramite un segnale condiviso.
it.extended_analysis: Con l'annuncio relativo alla gestione delle preferenze di addestramento tramite un segnale robots.txt condiviso, OpenAI cerca di semplificare la comunicazione tra i gestori dei siti web e i provider partecipanti. La descrizione fornita è tuttavia sintetica e non specifica quali provider aderiscano all'iniziativa né i dettagli tecnici completi dell'implementazione.
it.context: La gestione dei dati web per l'addestramento dei modelli di intelligenza artificiale rappresenta un tema centrale di dibattito tra editori, proprietari di siti e aziende tecnologiche.
key_takeaways: OpenAI honorerà un segnale robots.txt condiviso.
L'obiettivo è facilitare la comunicazione delle preferenze di addestramento IA.
L'iniziativa si rivolge ai siti web e ai provider partecipanti.
highlights: Segnale robots.txt condiviso per i siti web.

it.title: Rapporto sulla sicurezza della community e nuove tutele per i teenager
it.summary: OpenAI ha annunciato il rafforzamento della prevenzione della violenza all'interno di ChatGPT. L'aggiornamento introduce salvaguardie ampliate, interventi più tempestivi e un nuovo impegno per la rendicontazione pubblica sulla sicurezza. Queste misure mirano ad affrontare in modo più strutturato la protezione dei giovani utenti.
it.why_it_matters: Questi interventi affrontano direttamente la protezione dei minori e la prevenzione della violenza in un sistema di intelligenza artificiale ampiamente utilizzato. La pubblicazione di un report sulla sicurezza della community segnala una maggiore trasparenza nelle politiche di mitigazione dei rischi adottate da OpenAI.
it.extended_analysis:
Nel panorama attuale dell'intelligenza artificiale generativa, la sicurezza e la protezione dei minori sono diventate questioni centrali per gli sviluppatori e i regolatori. OpenAI ha risposto a queste esigenze annunciando nuove tutele per i teenager e un impegno formale nella reportistica di sicurezza.

Le modifiche descritte comprendono salvaguardie ampliate e meccanismi di intervento precoce integrati direttamente in ChatGPT. Queste misure sono progettate per intercettare e prevenire contenuti legati alla violenza, offrendo uno scudo protettivo più efficace per gli utenti più giovani.

Gli osservatori del settore e gli utenti dovranno monitorare l'efficacia pratica di queste misure, valutando come le nuove tutele si integreranno nell'esperienza quotidiana della piattaforma senza compromettere l'usabilità complessiva.
it.context: Il settore dell'intelligenza artificiale è sottoposto a crescenti pressioni per garantire ambienti sicuri, in particolare per i minori. L'adozione di report sulla sicurezza e di barriere protettive risponde alla necessità di regolamentazione e autoregolamentazione della tecnologia.
key_takeaways: OpenAI ha introdotto nuove tutele specifiche per i teenager su ChatGPT.
Le salvaguardie contro la violenza sono state ampliate con interventi più tempestivi.
È stato stabilito un nuovo impegno per la rendicontazione pubblica sulla sicurezza.
highlights: Annunciato un nuovo report sulla sicurezza della community da parte di OpenAI.
Implementate salvaguardie ampliate e interventi precoci per la prevenzione della violenza.

en.title: Community safety report and new protections for teens
en.summary: OpenAI is strengthening violence prevention in ChatGPT with expanded safeguards, earlier interventions, and a new commitment to public safety reporting. These updates aim to address safety concerns surrounding younger demographics and platform usage. The measures outline a structured approach to user protection and institutional transparency.
en.why_it_matters: Enhancing safety protocols for younger users is a critical challenge for widely deployed generative AI systems. By formalizing public safety reporting and earlier interventions, the initiative addresses growing societal expectations regarding platform accountability.
en.extended_analysis:
As generative artificial intelligence becomes deeply integrated into daily communication, safeguarding vulnerable populations like teenagers is a primary operational challenge. OpenAI's latest announcement focuses on reinforcing violence prevention mechanisms within ChatGPT through systematic updates.

The framework introduces expanded safeguards and earlier interventions designed to identify and mitigate potential risks before they escalate. Coupled with a public safety reporting commitment, these steps represent an effort to document platform safety developments transparently.

Evaluating the real-world impact of these safeguards will require ongoing observation of how well the early intervention mechanisms operate at scale. Stakeholders will be watching to see how OpenAI maintains the balance between protective barriers and the utility of the conversational model.
en.context: Public scrutiny regarding the impact of conversational AI on minors has intensified across global markets. Technology companies face increasing demands to implement verifiable safety architectures and transparent reporting standards.
key_takeaways: OpenAI rolled out expanded safeguards and earlier interventions for teens in ChatGPT.
The updates focus specifically on strengthening violence prevention mechanisms.
A new commitment to public safety reporting was introduced alongside the technical changes.
highlights: Expanded safeguards and early intervention systems implemented in ChatGPT.
New public safety reporting commitment established by OpenAI.

es.title: Informe de seguridad comunitaria y nuevas protecciones para adolescentes
es.summary: OpenAI ha anunciado un fortalecimiento de la prevención de la violencia en ChatGPT mediante salvaguardias ampliadas, intervenciones más tempranas y un nuevo compromiso con la presentación de informes de seguridad pública. Estas medidas buscan responder a los desafíos de protección de los usuarios jóvenes en plataformas de inteligencia artificial.
es.why_it_matters: La implementación de salvaguardias específicas para adolescentes y la mejora en la prevención de la violencia son aspectos cruciales para la adopción segura de la IA generativa. Este enfoque busca equilibrar la accesibilidad de la tecnología con la responsabilidad corporativa en materia de protección al usuario.
es.extended_analysis:
En el contexto actual de la inteligencia artificial conversacional, la seguridad de los menores se ha consolidado como una prioridad operativa. OpenAI ha respondido a estas demandas implementando un conjunto de medidas orientadas a proteger a los adolescentes que utilizan ChatGPT.

Las actualizaciones incluyen mecanismos de intervención temprana y salvaguardias ampliadas enfocadas en la prevención de la violencia. Estas herramientas técnicas se complementan con un compromiso formal hacia la transparencia mediante informes públicos de seguridad.

El éxito a largo plazo de estas iniciativas dependerá de su correcta ejecución y de la capacidad de adaptación frente a nuevos escenarios de riesgo. Los analistas y usuarios deberán seguir de cerca la evolución de estas políticas de protección en el ecosistema digital.
es.context: La presión social y regulatoria sobre los proveedores de inteligencia artificial para proteger a los usuarios vulnerables ha impulsado el desarrollo de nuevas normativas internas y estándares de transparencia en la industria tecnológica.
key_takeaways: OpenAI refuerza la prevención de la violencia en ChatGPT con nuevas salvaguardias.
Se introducen intervenciones más tempranas orientadas a la protección de los adolescentes.
Se establece un compromiso formal con la rendición de cuentas pública en seguridad.
highlights: Lanzamiento de nuevas protecciones para adolescentes en ChatGPT.
Implementación de un compromiso de informe de seguridad pública.

zh-CN.title: 社区安全报告与针对青少年的全新保护措施
zh-CN.summary: OpenAI正通过扩大安全防范、更早的干预机制以及对公共安全报告的新承诺，来加强ChatGPT中的暴力防范。这些更新旨在应对年轻用户群体在使用生成式人工智能时的安全隐患。此举标志着平台在提升透明度和落实用户保护方面迈出了一步。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 随着生成式人工智能的普及，针对未成年人的安全防护和暴力预防成为了技术部署的核心议题。通过引入早期干预和公开安全报告，OpenAI回应了社会各界对平台问责制和透明度的持续关注。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
在当前的生成式人工智能领域中，如何确保年轻用户的安全已成为开发商和监管机构共同面临的重大课题。OpenAI近期宣布了一系列旨在提升ChatGPT安全性的更新，重点关注青少年群体的保护。

此次发布的措施包括扩展的安全防范机制以及更早的干预手段，旨在识别并缓解潜在风险。结合对公共安全报告的全新承诺，这些举措旨在为平台的操作提供更为透明的记录。

技术观察人士和用户需要密切关注这些早期干预机制在实际应用中的表现，评估其在平衡模型效用与安全防护方面的效果。

key_takeaways: OpenAI在ChatGPT中推出了针对青少年的全新保护与防范措施。
通过扩展的安全防范机制加强了对暴力的预防。
建立了公开安全报告的新承诺以提升透明度。

实施了更早的干预机制与扩大的暴力防范 safeguards。

de.title: Community-Sicherheitsbericht und neue Schutzmaßnahmen für Jugendliche
de.summary: OpenAI verstärkt die Gewaltprävention in ChatGPT durch erweiterte Sicherheitsvorkehrungen, frühere Interventionen und eine neue Verpflichtung zur öffentlichen Sicherheitsberichterstattung. Diese Maßnahmen zielen darauf ab, den Schutz jüngerer Nutzer bei der Nutzung von KI-Plattformen zu verbessern. Gleichzeitig wird damit ein strukturierter Ansatz zur Transparenz verfolgt.

items.title: Building a multiplayer game world with autonomous Fable-class models
items.summary: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World Don't be put off by the clickbait headline, this piece by Jacob Sansbury describing how they are building Spawn is a fascinating exploration of the bleeding edge of what's possible with agentic engineering against frontier models. Spawn is a massively multiplayer gaming environment where players can use prompts (to the in-game agent, Savi) to modify the game world. I fired it up on my phone for a few minutes and was able to prompt a castle into existence, then a dragon, then ride the dragon to fly around that castle. By Jacob's telling, Spawn is now being developed autonomously by a swarm of Fable-powered agents costing over $3 million in tokens per month ("we spend 30x payroll on AI tokens"). Our agents change the live code directly and ship to production hourly, so they read every error, bug report and metric themselves. About 60% of our work starts from a production error, a Savi bug report (Savi is the AI you build games with in Spawn), something odd in our logs, or a feature request. Savi files bugs herself. When a user hits one, or Savi hits one in the product, she files it. It goes straight to an agent that decides whether it's a real bug to fix, something we won't fix, or intentional design that needs a decision. Usually it becomes a change, delivered to that user within an hour, with a message in the same chat. This is continuous deployment turned up to 11: A loop this tight only works if it never stops, so we treat an hour without a ship as a SEV-0, our most severe kind of incident. Unshipped changes pile up, and every problem already in production lasts longer. The feedback slows down too. An agent can only keep a few hours of work in its head, so shipping faster than that actually helps it stay coherent. [.

Introducing AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel: Open Models for Speech and Decisions on Apple Platforms
Quoting Ted Sanders
items.summary: In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. As you note, our models are ordered: Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra [ ... ] These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement. So something like 6.1 would indicate it was launched after 5.6, may share some similarities to other 6.1 models in terms of training data / personality (which is why it's not 5.7), and isn't a giant enough leap to merit the headlines and expectations that would come with a 7. — Ted Sanders , explaining OpenAI's model naming conventions Tags: generative-ai , gpt , openai , ai , llms , ted-sanders

it.title: Perché gli agenti IA amano Supabase
it.summary: In questo episodio di Latent Space, i cofondatori di Supabase Paul Copplestone e Ant Wilson discutono con swyx di come la programmazione guidata dagli agenti IA stia trasformando le esigenze dei database e dei backend.
it.why_it_matters: La crescente diffusione di software creato da agenti IA impone nuove sfide e funzionalità ai backend, come la gestione di carichi di lavoro a lungo termine e schemi più comprensibili.
it.extended_analysis:
Man mano che gli agenti IA assumono ruoli di rilievo nella creazione di software, le infrastrutture tradizionali devono adattarsi. La conversazione esplora le modifiche necessarie per consentire agli agenti di interagire in modo efficiente con i dati e i carichi di lavoro.

Vengono esaminate le soluzioni per affiancare carichi di lavoro persistenti direttamente al database e semplificare la struttura dei dati affinché i sistemi autonomi possano interpretarli senza ostacoli.

Nel contesto attuale dell'ingegneria del software, comprendere l'evoluzione dei backend orientati agli agenti è fondamentale per anticipare le tendenze dello sviluppo tecnologico.
it.context: L'episodio si inserisce nel dibattito in evoluzione sull'adattamento delle infrastrutture dati tradizionali alle nuove esigenze imposte dall'automazione avanzata e dalla generazione di codice tramite intelligenza artificiale.
key_takeaways: I carichi di lavoro a lungo termine richiedono nuove strategie di gestione accanto al database.
Gli schemi semplificati aiutano gli agenti IA a comprendere e scrivere software in modo efficace.
Il ruolo dei backend sta mutando per soddisfare le esigenze dei programmatori autonomi.
highlights: Ospiti: i cofondatori di Supabase Paul Copplestone e Ant Wilson.
Conduttore: swyx per il podcast Latent Space.

en.title: Why Agents Love Supabase
en.summary: In this Latent Space episode, Supabase co-founders Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson join swyx to discuss how AI agents are changing software creation and what backend systems need to do next.
en.why_it_matters: As AI agents build more software, backend requirements evolve to support long-lived workloads and make schemas easier for automated systems to understand.
en.extended_analysis:
The shift toward software generated by AI agents introduces distinct infrastructural challenges. This discussion unpacks how databases and backend platforms must evolve to accommodate persistent workloads running right alongside data stores.

Guests Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson share insights on structuring schemas so that automated agents can comprehend and manipulate them smoothly, pointing toward a future of agent-native infrastructure.

For developers and architects navigating the intersection of AI and databases, this conversation offers a focused look at shifting requirements in modern software design.
en.context: This discussion addresses the technical adjustments required when artificial intelligence takes a more active role in software development and code generation.
key_takeaways: AI agents are altering software creation habits and backend infrastructure demands.
Running long-lived workloads alongside databases becomes increasingly important.
Schemas must be designed for easier comprehension by automated agents.
highlights: Guests: Supabase co-founders Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson.
Host: swyx on Latent Space.

es.title: Por qué los agentes adoran Supabase
es.summary: En este episodio de Latent Space, los cofundadores de Supabase, Paul Copplestone y Ant Wilson, charlan con swyx sobre cómo los agentes de IA transforman la creación de software y los requisitos del backend.
es.why_it_matters: A medida que los agentes de infraestructura y código autónomo ganan terreno, las arquitecturas de backend deben adaptarse para gestionar cargas de trabajo persistentes y esquemas más claros.
es.extended_analysis:
La creación de software impulsada por agentes de inteligencia artificial exige un replanteamiento de las herramientas de desarrollo. La charla examina qué significa para un backend operar eficientemente en este nuevo paradigma.

Se abordan temas clave como la ejecución de cargas de trabajo de larga duración junto a la base de datos y la simplificación de esquemas para facilitar su lectura por parte de agentes automatizados.

Es una lectura analítica esencial para comprender la evolución de las plataformas de datos ante la automatización del desarrollo de software.
es.context: El episodio aborda los cambios técnicos que surgen cuando los sistemas de inteligencia artificial participan de forma directa en la producción de código y aplicaciones.
key_takeaways: Los agentes de IA modifican las necesidades técnicas de las plataformas backend.
Es vital ejecutar cargas de trabajo de larga duración junto con las bases de datos.
Los esquemas de datos simplificados mejoran la comprensión por parte de los agentes.
highlights: Invitados: los cofundadores de Supabase Paul Copplestone y Ant Wilson.
Presentador: swyx en Latent Space.

zh-CN.title: 为什么智能体钟爱 Supabase
zh-CN.summary: 在本期 Latent Space 节目中，Supabase 联合创始人 Paul Copplestone 和 Ant Wilson 与主持人 swyx 一起探讨了 AI 智能体如何改变软件开发以及后端需要做出的调整。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 随着 AI 智能体编写更多软件，后端需求随之演变，需要支持长期运行的工作负载并使数据架构更易于智能体理解。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
随着人工智能在软件生成中扮演越来越积极的角色，传统基础设施面临新的设计要求。本次对话探讨了数据库平台如何适应这一趋势。

访谈重点关注如何在数据库旁运行持久化工作负载，以及如何简化架构以便自动化系统能够顺畅解析和操作数据。

对于关注软件工程与人工智能交叉领域的开发者而言，这期节目提供了关于现代后端演进的深度行业视角。
zh-CN.context: 该对话聚焦于当人工智能更多参与软件开发时，底层数据基础设施所需的技术和架构调整。
key_takeaways: AI 智能体正在改变软件创造方式及后端架构需求。
在数据库旁运行长期工作负载变得更加关键。
必须设计更直观的架构，以便自动化智能体理解。

de.title: Warum KI-Agenten Supabase lieben
de.summary: In dieser Episode von Latent Space sprechen die Supabase-Mitgründer Paul Copplestone und Ant Wilson mit swyx darüber, wie KI-Agenten die Softwareentwicklung verändern und was Backends leisten müssen.
de.why_it_matters: Da KI-Agenten zunehmend Software erstellen, ändern sich die Anforderungen an Backends, um langlebige Workloads zu unterstützen und Datenstrukturen für Agenten verständlicher zu machen.
de.extended_analysis:
Die zunehmende Erstellung von Software durch künstliche Intelligenz erfordert ein Umdenken bei Infrastruktur und Datenhaltung. Die Diskussion beleuchtet, wie sich Backend-Systeme an diese neuen Gegebenheiten anpassen.

Thematisiert werden die Ausführung langlebiger Workloads direkt neben der Datenbank sowie die Vereinfachung von Schemata, damit automatisierte Agenten diese fehlerfrei interpretieren können.

Für Entwickler und Architekten bietet das Gespräch wertvolle Einblicke in die anstehenden Veränderungen moderner Software-Architekturen.
de.context: Die Episode beleuchtet die technischen und konzeptionellen Anpassungen, die durch den verstärkten Einsatz von KI in der Software-Erstellung notwendig werden.
key_takeaways: KI-Agenten verändern die Anforderungen an die Backend-Infrastruktur.
Langlebige Workloads müssen direkt neben der Datenbank ausgeführt werden.
Vereinfachte Schemata erleichtern automatisierten Systemen das Verständnis.
highlights: Gäste: Die Supabase-Mitgründer Paul Copplestone und Ant Wilson.
Host: swyx bei Latent Space.

it.title: La strategia ASI degli Stati Uniti con Joel Predd, Ben Boudreaux e Matt Chessen

Gli ospiti esaminano diversi archetipi strategici e sostengono l'importanza di preservare la libertà d'azione tramite capacità flessibili e a lungo termine.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere le dinamiche geopolitiche dell'ASI è fondamentale per valutare come le superpotenze affronteranno i futuri equilibri di potere tecnologico.
it.extended_analysis:
Il dibattito sulla superintelligenza artificiale non riguarda più soltanto i progressi dei laboratori di ricerca, ma entra a pieno titolo nelle agende della sicurezza nazionale e della geopolitica globale.

Nel corso della conversazione, gli esperti di RAND affrontano i nodi cruciali legati alla competizione strategica, esaminando i diversi approcci che gli Stati Uniti potrebbero adottare di fronte all'accelerazione tecnologica.

Vengono approfonditi concetti chiave come il mantenimento della libertà d'azione attraverso strumenti flessibili e investimenti a lungo termine, offrendo uno spunto di riflessione sulle implicazioni a lungo termine per le politiche pubbliche e la difesa.
it.context: La discussione si inserisce nel contesto della crescente competizione globale per lo sviluppo dell'intelligenza artificiale avanzata e delle relative strategie di sicurezza nazionale.
key_takeaways: Esame approfondito della strategia geopolitica degli Stati Uniti per l'ASI.
Analisi di archetipi strategici concorrenti nella corsa tecnologica.
Importanza di mantenere la libertà d'azione tramite capacità flessibili e a lungo termine.

en.title: Freedom of Action: America's ASI Strategy with RAND Experts

en.why_it_matters: Examining how geopolitical strategies adapt to the pursuit of artificial superintelligence provides crucial insight into future global power dynamics.

As the race for artificial superintelligence accelerates, policy and national security frameworks must adapt to unprecedented technological shifts. In this episode, researchers from RAND explore the complexities of US geopolitical strategy.

The discussion centers on competing strategic archetypes, evaluating how different approaches could shape the nation's posture in an increasingly uncertain technological landscape.

Listeners are provided with a structured look at why maintaining flexibility and long-lead capabilities is argued to be essential for preserving strategic freedom of action in the years ahead.

items.summary: GitHub Octoverse 2026 I'm at GitHub Universe today (GitHub gave me a free ticket through their "GitHub Stars" program). EVP Jay Parikh just announced this year's Octoverse report, and highlighted these numbers in particular: This is a pretty stark representation of the impact of agentic engineering on GitHub. In 2026, merged pull requests tripled in less than a year to 220 million per month. Commits more than tripled to 7.38 billion per month, with most of that increase in the second half of this year. New repository rate doubled this year, to 30.3 million per month. The report includes new numbers by industry, and breaks out numbers for repositories that involve "interoperability or reverse engineering". The methodology section includes notes about how they did this: Top countries by pushes to public repositories, adjusted by profile location . Pushes from each country were summed across the Octoverse year. To adjust for biases caused by VPN usage, LLM classification was used to extract the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code from the profiles of GitHub users who contributed pushes during this period [...] Industry . Public repositories created 2022 to 2026 were sorted into NAICS sectors by a fine-tuned multilingual embedding model using name, description, topics, and README, from random samples per year. [...] Interoperability . Counts public repositories created each year whose name, description, topics, or README mention interoperability or reverse engineering, or related terms, such as clean room implementation, drop-in replacement, or protocol re-implementation. items.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development
items.summary: I've written before about how November 2025 was an inflection point for coding agents - the point where Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 crossed a tipping point that meant their respective coding agents became reliable daily drivers for software engineers. I think we've reached a new inflection point in October 2026, and this time it's for vibe coding computer games . Tree Appreciator Emberwick Battle Drones Pumpkin Farmer, aka Quarter Sun Cove Four times as insulting What happens if someone actually puts the work in? You should build a game! Claude Opus 5.5 in particular exhibits meaningful improvements in several areas needed to build a compelling game: 3D modeling Music generation (see Scrimshaw Jukebox ) Game design (!) That last one is particularly important. Models have been able to create something that looks like a game for quite a while now, as seen in my previous experiments . The challenge has been getting to a game that's actually fun to play . Game design is a deep subject area. I won't pretend to be well versed in it - I know enough to have respect for it as a craft. Creating a novel, compelling gameplay loop which challenges players at the right level and provides a satisfying learning curve is a fine art. I didn't think the models could do it. Then I tried telling Claude Opus 5.5 to "Make it a LOT more fun"... and it did . In the past few weeks I've vibe coded (in the classic sense of the term - no looking at the code at all) four games that I've genuinely enjoyed playing. es.context: El podcast Latent Space explora de manera continuada las innovaciones en ingeniería de inteligencia artificial y su aplicación práctica. El episodio se enmarca en la discusión técnica sobre la evaluación y validación de modelos científicos.

zh-CN.why_it_matters: 为科学领域的AI工具开发可靠的评估方法，对于验证其在复杂研究中的实际能力至关重要。该节目凸显了业界在构建具备明确验证标准的基准测试方面的持续探索。

de.why_it_matters: Die Entwicklung verlässlicher Evaluierungsmethoden für KI-gestützte wissenschaftliche Werkzeuge ist entscheidend, um deren tatsächliche Leistungsfähigkeit zu überprüfen. de.extended_analysis:

items.title: AI:AM Highlights: Clean Neurons, Black October, the GPU Credit Crunch, and Buying the Supply Chain
items.summary: Nathan Labenz and Prakash Narayanan examine what dictates the pace of AI development with guests Zvi Mowshowitz, Evan Conrad, and Lonis Hamaili. The discussions cover rapid capability timelines, credit constraints in compute financing, and supply chain bottlenecks.
items.podcastDescription: Conversazioni su capacità emergenti, ricerca e impatto dell'intelligenza artificiale.

it.title: I punti di svolta dell'IA: crediti GPU, catene di approvvigionamento e tempistiche
it.summary: In questo episodio, Nathan Labenz e Prakash Narayanan analizzano i fattori che guidano il ritmo dello sviluppo dell'intelligenza artificiale insieme agli ospiti Zvi Mowshowitz, Evan Conrad e Lonis Hamaili. Al centro del dibattito ci sono le tempistiche di crescita delle capacità, le restrizioni di credito nel finanziamento di calcolo e i colli di bottiglia della catena di fornitura.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere le dinamiche finanziarie e logistiche dietro l'hardware e i crediti GPU è essenziale per decifrare l'effettiva evoluzione industriale dell'IA.
it.extended_analysis:
L'episodio approfondisce i meccanismi critici che regolano l'industria dell'intelligenza artificiale, focalizzandosi su come le limitazioni finanziarie e di approvvigionamento influenzino la ricerca e la scalabilità dei modelli. Vengono esaminati i vincoli legati ai crediti di calcolo e l'impatto delle catene di fornitura globali sullo sviluppo tecnologico.

Attraverso il confronto tra i conduttori e gli ospiti, emergono prospettive concrete sulle sfide infrastrutturali che il settore deve affrontare per sostenere il proprio ritmo di crescita, offrendo una visione approfondita dei fattori economici e materiali che plasmano il futuro dell'IA.
it.context: Il dibattito si inserisce nel contesto delle crescenti pressioni economiche e infrastrutturali che caratterizzano l'industria dell'intelligenza artificiale, dove l'accesso a risorse di calcolo avanzate e a una catena di fornitura stabile rappresenta un vantaggio competitivo cruciale.
key_takeaways: Analisi dei fattori che determinano il ritmo dello sviluppo dell'IA.
Esame dei vincoli di credito nel finanziamento delle risorse di calcolo.
Discussione sui colli di bottiglia della catena di fornitura e delle tempistiche di capability.
highlights: Ospiti della puntata: Zvi Mowshowitz, Evan Conrad e Lonis Hamaili.
Conduzione affidata a Nathan Labenz e Prakash Narayanan.

en.title: AI:AM Highlights: Clean Neurons, GPU Credits, and Supply Chain Realities
en.summary: Nathan Labenz and Prakash Narayanan examine what dictates the pace of AI development with guests Zvi Mowshowitz, Evan Conrad, and Lonis Hamaili. The discussions cover rapid capability timelines, credit constraints in compute financing, and supply chain bottlenecks.
en.why_it_matters: Examining the financial and logistical bottlenecks behind compute infrastructure sheds light on the true mechanics driving the artificial intelligence industry forward.
en.extended_analysis:
This episode delivers a targeted examination of the underlying mechanics shaping artificial intelligence progress, moving beyond software to address the hard economic and material realities. The discussion tackles how financing constraints and compute credits directly influence development velocity.

By engaging with specialists Zvi Mowshowitz, Evan Conrad, and Lonis Hamaili, the hosts unpack complex supply chain dynamics and capability timelines, offering listeners a structured view of the structural hurdles facing large-scale AI deployment.
en.context: As artificial intelligence systems scale in size and demand, the industry faces unprecedented scrutiny regarding hardware supply chains, compute financing structures, and the economic sustainability of rapid capability growth.
key_takeaways: Exploration of rapid capability timelines and development pacing.
Analysis of credit constraints impacting compute financing.
Detailed look at ongoing supply chain bottlenecks in hardware.
highlights: Featuring insights from Zvi Mowshowitz, Evan Conrad, and Lonis Hamaili.
Hosted by Nathan Labenz and Prakash Narayanan.

es.title: Aspectos destacados de la IA: créditos de GPU, cadena de suministro y plazos
es.summary: Nathan Labenz y Prakash Narayanan examinan los factores que dictan el ritmo del desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial junto a los invitados Zvi Mowshowitz, Evan Conrad y Lonis Hamaili. Las conversaciones abordan los plazos de capacidades rápidas, las restricciones de crédito en la financiación de computación y los cuellos de botella en la cadena de suministro.
es.why_it_matters: Comprender los límites financieros y logísticos de la infraestructura de computación ayuda a descifrar los verdaderos desafíos de la industria de la IA.
es.extended_analysis:
El episodio analiza los elementos críticos que determinan la velocidad de avance en el sector de la inteligencia artificial, prestando especial atención a las limitaciones financieras y materiales. Se discute cómo las restricciones en los créditos de computación y la cadena de suministro afectan directamente la viabilidad de los proyectos a gran escala.

A través del intercambio con los invitados, se ofrece una perspectiva detallada sobre los obstáculos estructurales que enfrenta el ecosistema tecnológico, permitiendo a los oyentes evaluar con mayor rigor las dinámicas económicas del sector.
es.context: El debate refleja las tensiones actuales en el ecosistema tecnológico, donde la creciente demanda de potencia de cálculo choca con la realidad financiera y las limitaciones logísticas de la cadena de suministro global.
key_takeaways: Evaluación de los plazos de desarrollo y las capacidades de la IA.
Análisis de las restricciones de crédito en la financiación del cálculo.
Discusión sobre los cuellos de botella en la cadena de suministro.
highlights: Participación de los invitados Zvi Mowshowitz, Evan Conrad y Lonis Hamaili.
Conducción a cargo de Nathan Labenz y Prakash Narayanan.

zh-CN.title: AI:AM焦点：清洁神经元、GPU信贷紧缩与供应链瓶颈

zh-CN.why_it_matters: 深入了解算力基础设施背后的金融与物流现实，有助于揭示推动人工智能行业前进的真实机制。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
本期节目聚焦于塑造人工智能发展的底层硬件与经济现实，超越了单纯的技术层面。主持人与多位嘉宾共同探讨了融资限制和算力信贷如何直接影响研发速度与规模化进程。

通过对供应链动态和能力时间表的梳理，节目为听众提供了一个清晰的框架，用于审视大规模人工智能部署所面临的结构性挑战与经济考验。
zh-CN.context: 随着人工智能系统的规模不断扩大，行业正面临前所未有的审视，重点聚焦于硬件供应链、算力融资结构以及快速能力增长的经济可持续性。
key_takeaways: 探讨快速能力时间表与研发节奏。
分析影响算力融资的信贷限制。
审视当前硬件供应链中的各类瓶颈。
highlights: 特邀嘉宾包括Zvi Mowshowitz、Evan Conrad和Lonis Hamaili。
由Nathan Labenz和Prakash Narayanan主持。

de.title: AI:AM-Highlights: GPU-Kreditklemme, Lieferketten und Entwicklungstempo
de.summary: Nathan Labenz und Prakash Narayanan untersuchen gemeinsam mit den Gästen Zvi Mowshowitz, Evan Conrad und Lonis Hamaili, was das Tempo der KI-Entwicklung bestimmt. Die Diskussionen behandeln schnelle Fähigkeitszeitpläne, Kreditbeschränkungen bei der Rechenfinanzierung und Lieferkettenengpässe.
de.why_it_matters: Die Beleuchtung der finanzellen und logistischen Engpässe hinter der Recheninfrastruktur verdeutlicht die wahren Mechanismen, die die KI-Industrie antreiben.
de.extended_analysis:
Diese Episode widmet sich den grundlegenden wirtschaftlichen und materiellen Realitäten, die den Fortschritt der künstlichen Intelligenz prägen. Die Diskussion beleuchtet, wie Finanzierungsbeschränkungen und Rechenkredite die Entwicklungsgeschwindigkeit direkt beeinflussen.

Durch den Austausch mit den Gästen analysieren die Moderatoren komplexe Lieferkettendynamiken und Zeitpläne, um den Hörern einen fundierten Einblick in die strukturellen Hürden zu geben, denen sich die Branche gegenüber sieht.
de.context: Vor dem Hintergrund des rasanten Wachstums von KI-Systemen steht die Branche vor wachsenden wirtschaftlichen und infrastrukturellen Herausforderungen, bei denen der Zugang zu Rechenleistung und stabilen Lieferketten entscheidend ist.
key_takeaways: Untersuchung von Fähigkeitszeitplänen und Entwicklungstempo.
Analyse von Kreditbeschränkungen bei der Finanzierung von Rechenleistung.
Detaillierte Betrachtung von Lieferkettenengpässen in der Hardware.
highlights: Mit Beiträgen der Gäste Zvi Mowshowitz, Evan Conrad und Lonis Hamaili.
Moderiert von Nathan Labenz und Prakash Narayanan.

it.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro punta su contesto lungo e pesi aperti
it.summary: Moonshot presenta Kimi K3.1 Pro, un modello open-weight da 3 trilioni di parametri con una finestra di contesto da un milione di token. La variante Highspeed promette una velocità 2–3 volte maggiore; l’azienda annuncia il rilascio dei pesi completi entro il 4 novembre. I benchmark pubblicati sono risultati dichiarati da Moonshot, da confrontare con test indipendenti.
it.why_it_matters: Un modello di queste dimensioni, con pesi destinati alla pubblicazione, può ampliare la sperimentazione su coding e agenti. Il valore pratico dipenderà però da licenza, requisiti hardware e verifiche indipendenti, non solo dai benchmark del produttore.
it.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro è il nuovo modello di punta annunciato da Moonshot AI. La società lo descrive come un sistema open-weight da 3T di parametri, capace di gestire fino a un milione di token di contesto. Accanto alla versione standard arriva K3.1 Pro Highspeed, presentata come 2–3 volte più veloce.

La pagina ufficiale riporta risultati su coding, ricerca finanziaria e attività agentiche, tra cui 65,7% su Terminal-Bench 4.0. Sono valutazioni comunicate dal produttore: per capire quanto siano riproducibili servono pesi, metodologia completa e confronti indipendenti. Moonshot indica il 4 novembre per la pubblicazione dei pesi completi; sarà quello il passaggio decisivo per valutare accessibilità, costi di esecuzione e possibilità di adattamento.
it.context: I modelli open-weight permettono a sviluppatori e organizzazioni di esaminare e distribuire i pesi, entro i termini della licenza. Una finestra di contesto molto ampia è utile per documenti e flussi di lavoro lunghi, ma aumenta anche i requisiti di memoria e calcolo.
key_takeaways: Contesto dichiarato: fino a 1 milione di token.
La variante Highspeed promette 2–3× la velocità.
Pesi completi annunciati entro il 4 novembre; benchmark da verificare indipendentemente.
highlights: Modello open-weight da 3T di parametri, secondo Moonshot.
Disponibile anche una variante Highspeed.
I risultati citati provengono dalla valutazione pubblicata dall’azienda.

en.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro pushes long context and open weights
en.summary: Moonshot introduces Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 3-trillion-parameter open-weight model with a one-million-token context window. Its Highspeed variant is claimed to run 2–3 times faster, while full weights are scheduled for release by November 4. The published benchmark figures are company-reported results and still need independent scrutiny.
en.why_it_matters: A model of this scale, with weights intended for release, could broaden experimentation in coding and agent workflows. Its practical value will depend on licensing, hardware requirements and independent evaluation—not just the vendor’s benchmarks.
en.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro is the new flagship model announced by Moonshot AI. The company describes it as a 3T-parameter open-weight system with a context window of up to one million tokens. A Highspeed variant is also offered, with a claimed 2–3× speed improvement.

The official post reports results across coding, financial research and agentic tasks, including 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0. These are figures published by the vendor; reproducibility will depend on the released weights, full methodology and independent comparisons. Moonshot says the complete weights are due by November 4. That release will be the real test of accessibility, serving costs and how easily developers can adapt the model.
en.context: Open-weight models let developers and organisations inspect and run model weights, subject to the licence. Very long context can help with large documents and multi-step workflows, but it also raises memory and compute demands.
key_takeaways: Advertised context window: up to one million tokens.
Highspeed is claimed to be 2–3× faster.
Full weights are expected by November 4; benchmarks remain vendor-reported.
highlights: A 3T-parameter open-weight model, according to Moonshot.
A faster Highspeed variant is also announced.
Published performance figures have not been independently validated here.

es.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro apuesta por contexto largo y pesos abiertos
es.summary: Moonshot presenta Kimi K3.1 Pro, un modelo de pesos abiertos de 3 billones de parámetros y una ventana de contexto de un millón de tokens. La variante Highspeed promete ser entre 2 y 3 veces más rápida; la empresa prevé publicar los pesos completos antes del 4 de noviembre. Las cifras de rendimiento difundidas son datos del fabricante y requieren comprobación independiente.
es.why_it_matters: Un modelo de esta escala, con pesos destinados a publicarse, puede ampliar la experimentación en programación y agentes. Su utilidad real dependerá de la licencia, el hardware necesario y las evaluaciones independientes, no solo de los benchmarks de la empresa.
es.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro es el nuevo modelo insignia anunciado por Moonshot AI. La compañía lo describe como un sistema de pesos abiertos de 3T de parámetros, con una ventana de contexto de hasta un millón de tokens. También presenta una variante Highspeed, a la que atribuye una velocidad entre dos y tres veces superior.

La publicación oficial recoge resultados en programación, investigación financiera y tareas con agentes, incluido un 65,7 % en Terminal-Bench 4.0. Son cifras comunicadas por el fabricante: su reproducibilidad dependerá de los pesos publicados, de la metodología completa y de comparaciones independientes. Moonshot anuncia los pesos completos para el 4 de noviembre; ese lanzamiento permitirá evaluar mejor el acceso, el coste de ejecución y la adaptación del modelo.
es.context: Los modelos de pesos abiertos permiten examinar y ejecutar los pesos, siempre dentro de las condiciones de su licencia. Un contexto muy amplio puede ayudar con documentos extensos y procesos de varios pasos, pero también exige más memoria y capacidad de cálculo.
key_takeaways: Contexto anunciado de hasta un millón de tokens.
Highspeed promete entre 2 y 3 veces más velocidad.
Los pesos completos se esperan para el 4 de noviembre; los benchmarks son del fabricante.
highlights: Modelo de pesos abiertos de 3T parámetros, según Moonshot.
Se anuncia una variante Highspeed.
Los resultados publicados aún necesitan validación independiente.

zh-CN.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro 将长上下文与开放权重推向新阶段
zh-CN.summary: Moonshot 发布 Kimi K3.1 Pro：一款拥有 3 万亿参数、支持 100 万 token 上下文窗口的开放权重模型。公司称 Highspeed 版本速度可提升 2–3 倍，并计划在 11 月 4 日前公开完整权重。现有基准成绩来自厂商公布，仍需独立评测验证。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 如果完整权重按计划开放，开发者将有更多机会测试和调整这一模型，用于编程与智能体工作流。实际价值仍取决于许可条款、硬件需求以及独立测试结果。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
Moonshot AI 将 Kimi K3.1 Pro 定位为新的旗舰模型。按照官方介绍，它采用开放权重，参数规模为 3T，上下文窗口最高可达 100 万 token。公司还推出 Highspeed 版本，并称其速度是标准版的 2–3 倍。

官方文章公布了编程、金融研究和智能体任务方面的成绩，其中包括 Terminal-Bench 4.0 的 65.7%。这些数字属于厂商披露的数据，是否能复现还要看完整权重、评测方法和第三方对比。Moonshot 表示完整权重预计于 11 月 4 日前发布；届时才能更准确地评估模型的可获得性、运行成本和可定制程度。
zh-CN.context: 开放权重模型允许开发者在许可范围内检查和运行模型权重。超长上下文有助于处理大型文档和多步骤任务，但通常也会提高内存与计算资源需求。
key_takeaways: 官方宣称上下文窗口最高达 100 万 token。
Highspeed 版本据称快 2–3 倍。
完整权重预计 11 月 4 日前发布；基准成绩仍待独立验证。
highlights: Moonshot 称该模型规模为 3T 参数。
同时推出 Highspeed 版本。
目前公布的性能数据来自厂商自身评测。

de.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro setzt auf langen Kontext und offene Gewichte
de.summary: Moonshot stellt Kimi K3.1 Pro vor: ein Open-Weight-Modell mit 3 Billionen Parametern und einem Kontextfenster von einer Million Tokens. Die Highspeed-Variante soll zwei- bis dreimal schneller sein; die vollständigen Gewichte sollen bis zum 4. November folgen. Die veröffentlichten Benchmarkwerte stammen vom Anbieter und müssen unabhängig überprüft werden.
de.why_it_matters: Ein Modell dieser Größe mit frei verfügbaren Gewichten könnte Experimente mit Coding und Agenten-Workflows erleichtern. Der praktische Nutzen hängt jedoch von Lizenz, Hardwarebedarf und unabhängigen Tests ab – nicht allein von den Benchmarks des Herstellers.
de.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro ist das neue Spitzenmodell, das Moonshot AI angekündigt hat. Das Unternehmen beschreibt es als Open-Weight-System mit 3 Billionen Parametern und einem Kontextfenster von bis zu einer Million Tokens. Zusätzlich gibt es eine Highspeed-Version, die laut Anbieter zwei- bis dreimal schneller arbeitet.

Der offizielle Beitrag nennt Ergebnisse für Coding, Finanzrecherche und agentische Aufgaben, darunter 65,7 Prozent auf Terminal-Bench 4.0. Diese Zahlen wurden vom Hersteller veröffentlicht; ihre Reproduzierbarkeit hängt von den verfügbaren Gewichten, der vollständigen Methodik und unabhängigen Vergleichen ab. Moonshot stellt die vollständigen Gewichte bis zum 4. November in Aussicht. Erst dann lassen sich Zugänglichkeit, Betriebskosten und Anpassungsmöglichkeiten besser beurteilen.
de.context: Open-Weight-Modelle erlauben Entwicklern und Organisationen, Gewichte im Rahmen der Lizenz zu prüfen und auszuführen. Ein sehr langes Kontextfenster hilft bei großen Dokumenten und mehrstufigen Aufgaben, erhöht aber auch den Speicher- und Rechenbedarf.
key_takeaways: Angegebenes Kontextfenster: bis zu einer Million Tokens.
Highspeed soll zwei- bis dreimal schneller sein.
Vollständige Gewichte bis 4. November angekündigt; Benchmarks sind Anbieterangaben.
highlights: Laut Moonshot ein Open-Weight-Modell mit 3T Parametern.
Zusätzliche Highspeed-Variante angekündigt.
Die veröffentlichten Leistungswerte benötigen unabhängige Bestätigung.

items.title: Airbnb Is Building a ‘Company Brain’ for AI Agents with Ahmad Al-Dahle - #781
items.summary: AI agents need the institutional knowledge experienced employees rely on: why a system works a certain way, which policies apply, and what never made it into the documentation. Capturing that knowledge is hard. Keeping it useful as people and agents add more may be harder. In this episode, Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO of Airbnb, shares how his team is building Project Everest, a “company brain” that captures knowledge from employees’ workflows for AI agents. We explore stale information and context poisoning, why too much context can backfire, and how the team evaluates whether shared knowledge improves engineering work. We also discuss measuring AI productivity beyond token usage and PR counts, the limits of chat-based interfaces, and deploying support agents in a marketplace where resolving disputes means mediating between conflicting interests. 🗒️ Full show notes: https://twimlai.com/go/781.

it.title: Airbnb e il 'cervello aziendale' per gli agenti IA
it.summary: In questo episodio, Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO di Airbnb, illustra Project Everest, un sistema progettato per catturare la conoscenza istituzionale dai flussi di lavoro dei dipendenti e metterla a disposizione degli agenti IA. L'episodio approfondisce le sfide legate alla gestione delle informazioni obsolete e del contesto in eccesso.
it.why_it_matters: Catturare la conoscenza non documentata è cruciale per permettere agli agenti IA di operare efficacemente in contesti aziendali complessi, evitando problemi legati all'affidabilità delle informazioni.
it.extended_analysis:
Gli agenti IA dipendono spesso dalla conoscenza tacita che i dipendenti esperti accumulano nel tempo, la quale raramente entra a far parte della documentazione ufficiale. Airbnb sta affrontando questa sfida con Project Everest, un'infrastruttura pensata per raccogliere e organizzare tale sapere aziendale.

Durante la conversazione, vengono esaminati i rischi derivanti da informazioni obsolete e dal fenomeno del 'context poisoning', in cui una quantità eccessiva o scorretta di dati può compromettere le prestazioni dei sistemi intelligenti. Vengono inoltre analizzati i metodi per valutare l'impatto reale del lavoro ingegneristico e le limitazioni delle interfacce basate su chat.
it.context: Nel panorama tecnologico attuale, le aziende cercano di andare oltre i semplici assistenti conversazionali, puntando su agenti autonomi capaci di integrarsi nei processi operativi quotidiani e di mediare in scenari complessi.
key_takeaways: Project Everest raccoglie la conoscenza aziendale nascosta nei flussi di lavoro per gli agenti IA.
Il 'context poisoning' e la gestione di informazioni obsolete rappresentano ostacoli significativi.
La misurazione della produttività dell'IA richiede metriche che vanno oltre i token o il conteggio delle PR.
highlights: Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO di Airbnb, è ospite dell'episodio.
Si discute dell'impiego di agenti di supporto in un mercato basato sulla mediazione di dispute.

en.title: Airbnb's Company Brain for AI Agents with Ahmad Al-Dahle
en.summary: In this episode, Airbnb CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle discusses Project Everest, a system designed to capture institutional knowledge from employee workflows for AI agents. The conversation explores stale information, context poisoning, and evaluating shared knowledge in engineering.
en.why_it_matters: Equipping AI agents with institutional knowledge is essential for effective deployment, yet capturing and maintaining accurate context remains a major technical challenge.
en.extended_analysis:
AI agents frequently lack the unwritten institutional knowledge that experienced employees rely on daily, from policy nuances to undocumented system behaviors. Airbnb's Project Everest aims to bridge this gap by capturing workflow insights directly from staff.

The discussion covers the complexities of maintaining relevance, avoiding context poisoning where excess data backfires, and evaluating whether shared knowledge genuinely enhances engineering output. Additional topics include measuring AI productivity beyond simplistic metrics and deploying marketplace support agents.
en.context: As organizations shift from basic chat assistants to autonomous AI agents, providing reliable internal data and managing information overload have become critical bottlenecks.
key_takeaways: Project Everest serves as a 'company brain' to supply AI agents with workflow knowledge.
Managing stale information and context overload prevents system backfires.
Evaluating AI productivity requires moving beyond traditional metrics like token usage and PR counts.
highlights: Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO of Airbnb, shares insights on building internal AI systems.
The episode examines marketplace dispute mediation using automated support agents.

es.title: El cerebro de empresa de Airbnb para agentes de IA
es.summary: En este episodio, Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO de Airbnb, analiza Project Everest, un sistema que recopila conocimiento institucional de los flujos de trabajo de los empleados para los agentes de IA. Se examinan los datos obsoletos, el envenenamiento de contexto y la medición de la productividad.
es.why_it_matters: Dotar a los agentes de IA de conocimientos no documentados es clave para su éxito operativo, pero mantener la información útil y actualizada plantea grandes retos.
es.extended_analysis:
Los agentes de IA necesitan comprender los matices internos y las políticas que los empleados experimentados conocen de forma intuitiva. Para resolverlo, Airbnb ha desarrollado Project Everest, un sistema destinado a capturar el conocimiento directamente de las tareas cotidianas.

El debate aborda los riesgos del exceso de contexto y la información desactualizada, así como las formas de evaluar si el conocimiento compartido mejora el trabajo de ingeniería. También se discuten los límites de las interfaces de chat y la implementación de agentes de soporte en mercados complejos.
es.context: La transición hacia agentes de IA autónomos en entornos empresariales exige resolver cómo las máquinas procesan y validan la información interna sin perder precisión.
key_takeaways: Project Everest captura el conocimiento de los flujos de trabajo para alimentar a los agentes de IA.
El exceso de contexto y la información obsoleta pueden reducir la eficacia del sistema.
Se exploran formas avanzadas de medir la productividad de la IA más allá de las métricas básicas.
highlights: Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO de Airbnb, participa como invitado en el episodio.
Se aborda el uso de agentes de soporte en la resolución de disputas de mercado.

zh-CN.title: 爱彼迎利用 Project Everest 为 AI 代理打造“公司大脑”
zh-CN.summary: 在本期节目中，爱彼迎首席技术官 Ahmad Al-Dahle 探讨了 Project Everest，这是一个旨在从员工工作流程中捕捉机构知识以供 AI 代理使用的系统。讨论内容涵盖过时信息、上下文污染以及评估工程共享知识。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 为 AI 代理提供未公开的机构知识对于其有效运作至关重要，但如何捕捉并维护准确的上下文仍然是一项重大的技术挑战。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
AI 代理通常缺乏经验丰富的员工所依赖的隐性机构知识，例如政策细微差别和未文档化的系统行为。爱彼迎的 Project Everest 旨在通过直接从员工的工作流程中收集见解来弥补这一差距。

讨论还涉及维护相关性的复杂性、避免因数据过多而适得其反的“上下文污染”，以及评估共享知识是否真正提升了工程产出。其他议题包括超越传统指标来衡量 AI 生产力，以及在市场环境中部署支持代理。
zh-CN.context: 随着企业从基础聊天助手向自主 AI 代理转型，提供可靠的内部数据并管理信息过载已成为关键瓶颈。
key_takeaways: Project Everest 作为“公司大脑”，为 AI 代理提供工作流程知识。
管理过时信息和上下文过载可防止系统产生负面效果。
评估 AI 生产力需要超越代数使用量和 PR 计数等传统指标。
highlights: 爱彼迎 CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle 分享了构建内部 AI 系统的见解。
节目探讨了在涉及各方利益冲突的市场中使用自动化支持代理进行争议调解。

de.title: Airbnbs Firmengehirn für KI-Agenten mit Ahmad Al-Dahle
de.summary: In dieser Episode bespricht Airbnb-CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle Project Everest, ein System zur Erfassung institutioneller Wissensbestände aus Mitarbeiter-Workflows für KI-Agenten. Themen sind Veraltung, Kontext-Vergiftung und die Evaluierung geteilten Wissens.
de.why_it_matters: KI-Agenten mit implizitem Unternehmenswissen auszustatten ist entscheidend für den Praxiseinsatz, doch die Pflege akkurater Kontexte stellt Entwickler vor enorme Herausforderungen.
de.extended_analysis:
KI-Agenten verfügen oft nicht über das unausgesprochene institutionelle Wissen erfahrener Mitarbeiter, wie Richtliniennuancen oder undokumentierte Systemabläufe. Airbnbs Project Everest soll diese Lücke schließen, indem Workflow-Erkenntnisse direkt erfasst werden.

Die Diskussion beleuchtet die Komplexität bei der Vermeidung veralteter Informationen und von 'Context Poisoning', bei dem überschüssige Daten die Leistung verschlechtern. Zudem werden die Messung echter KI-Produktivität jenseits einfacher Metriken sowie der Einsatz von Support-Agenten in umstrittenen Marktplatz-Szenarien erörtert.
de.context: Während Unternehmen von einfachen Chat-Assistenten zu autonomen KI-Agenten übergehen, entwickelt sich die Bereitstellung verlässlicher interner Daten zu einem zentralen Engpass.
key_takeaways: Project Everest dient als Firmengehirn zur Bereitstellung von Workflow-Wissen für KI-Agenten.
Die Handhabung veralteter Informationen verhindert negative Systemrückkopplungen.
Die Messung der KI-Produktivität erfordert Metriken jenseits von Token-Nutzung und Pull Requests.
highlights: Airbnb-CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle ist zu Gast in der Episode.
Es wird der Einsatz von Support-Agenten zur Vermittlung in Marktplatz-Streitigkeiten diskutiert.

it.title: Un mondo virtuale per la vita con Alex Rives di Biohub
it.summary: In questo episodio, il podcast The Cognitive Revolution ospita Alex Rives, Head of Science di Biohub ed ex cofondatore di Evolutionary Scale. Si discute di modelli di mondo biologici, celle virtuali e di una spinta sui dati da 1,8 miliardi di dollari.
it.why_it_matters: L'intervista esplora l'intersezione tra intelligenza artificiale e biologia, offrendo spunti sul futuro della ricerca scientifica avanzata e sui modelli computazionali applicati alla vita.
it.extended_analysis:
Il panorama dell'intelligenza artificiale applicata alle scienze della vita si arricchisce di nuove prospettive grazie al lavoro di Biohub, l'iniziativa supportata dal Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. Alex Rives condivide la sua esperienza nella creazione di modelli biologici avanzati, precedentemente sviluppati con la serie ESM di Evolutionary Scale.

La discussione si concentra sul potenziale delle celle virtuali e sulla misurazione dei dati su larga scala. Con un focus su una spinta economica e di dati imponente, l'episodio analizza come i modelli predittivi stiano cambiando l'approccio alla cura e alla comprensione dei sistemi biologici complessi.
it.context: La convergenza tra machine learning e biologia computazionale sta accelerando la ricerca in ambito medico e scientifico, aprendo nuove strade per la modellazione di sistemi viventi complessi.
key_takeaways: Il ruolo di Alex Rives come Head of Science a Biohub.
L'applicazione dei modelli di mondo alla biologia e alle celle virtuali.
Il contesto della ricerca supportata dal Chan Zuckerberg Initiative.
highlights: Ospite: Alex Rives, Head of Science presso Biohub ed ex cofondatore di Evolutionary Scale.
Argomenti chiave: modelli di mondo biologici, serie ESM e iniziative sui dati.

en.title: A World Model of Life with Biohub's Alex Rives
en.summary: In this episode of The Cognitive Revolution, host welcomes Alex Rives, Head of Science at Biohub and former co-founder of Evolutionary Scale. The discussion covers biological world models, virtual cells, and a major data initiative.
en.why_it_matters: Understanding how artificial intelligence models biological systems provides a glimpse into the future of biomedical research and computational science.
en.extended_analysis:
As artificial intelligence increasingly intersects with the life sciences, projects like those at Biohub—backed by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative—are pushing the boundaries of what computational models can achieve. Alex Rives brings deep expertise from his previous work on the ESM series of models at Evolutionary Scale.

The conversation highlights the conceptual framework behind virtual cells and large-scale biological measurement. Listeners gain insight into the ambitions driving modern biotechnology and the integration of data-heavy models into fundamental science.
en.context: The integration of advanced machine learning techniques into biological research represents a major frontier in modern scientific exploration and data-driven discovery.
key_takeaways: Insights from Alex Rives on biological world models.
The vision and scope of Biohub's scientific initiatives.
Discussion on virtual cells and large-scale data measurement.
highlights: Featured guest: Alex Rives, Head of Science at Biohub.
Topics include Evolutionary Scale's ESM models and data-driven biological research.

es.title: Un modelo mundial de la vida con Alex Rives de Biohub
es.summary: En este episodio de The Cognitive Revolution, el invitado es Alex Rives, Head of Science en Biohub y ex cofundador de Evolutionary Scale. Se examinan los modelos mundiales biológicos, las células virtuales y una gran iniciativa de datos.
es.why_it_matters: La intersección entre la inteligencia artificial y la biología computacional está redefiniendo los límites de la investigación científica avanzada y el modelado de sistemas vivos.
es.extended_analysis:
El desarrollo de modelos de inteligencia artificial aplicados a la biología abre nuevas vías para comprender sistemas complejos. Biohub, respaldado por la Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, busca abordar misiones ambiciosas en el ámbito de la salud y la ciencia.

Alex Rives comparte su trayectoria desde Evolutionary Scale, creadores de la serie de modelos ESM, hasta su rol actual. La conversación aborda cómo la medición de datos a gran escala y las células virtuales podrían transformar la investigación biomédica.
es.context: La aplicación de modelos computacionales avanzados a la biología celular y molecular refleja una tendencia creciente hacia la ciencia basada en datos masivos.
key_takeaways: La trayectoria y perspectiva de Alex Rives en biología computacional.
El enfoque de Biohub hacia la cura y el análisis de sistemas biológicos.
El impacto de los modelos de series ESM en la ciencia moderna.
highlights: Invitado: Alex Rives, Head of Science en Biohub y cofundador de Evolutionary Scale.
Temas principales: modelos mundiales de vida, células virtuales y datos.

zh-CN.title: 探索生命的生物世界模型：对话 Biohub 的 Alex Rives
zh-CN.summary: 在本期播客中，The Cognitive Revolution 迎来了 Biohub 科学负责人兼 Evolutionary Scale 联合创始人 Alex Rives。节目深入探讨了生物世界模型、虚拟细胞以及相关的大规模数据推动计划。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 人工智能与生物学的深度结合正在为生物医学研究和计算科学的未来提供全新视角，展现了数据驱动科学的巨大潜力。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
随着人工智能在生命科学领域的应用不断深入，由陈·扎克伯格倡议（Chan Zuckerberg Initiative）支持的 Biohub 正在探索前沿的科学任务。Alex Rives 结合其在 Evolutionary Scale 从事 ESM 系列模型开发的经验，分享了关于生物世界模型的构想。

对话重点关注了虚拟细胞的概念以及大规模数据测量在科学探索中的应用。听众可以从中了解到现代生物技术的发展方向以及计算模型如何助力基础科学研究。
zh-CN.context: 机器学习技术在生物研究中的广泛应用，标志着现代科学探索正在向数据密集型和计算驱动型方向加速转型。
key_takeaways: Alex Rives 谈生物世界模型与虚拟细胞的发展。
Biohub 在科学研究与数据推动方面的使命。
回顾 ESM 系列模型的应用与背景。
highlights: 特邀嘉宾：Biohub 科学负责人 Alex Rives。
讨论涵盖生物世界模型、虚拟细胞及大规模数据计划。

de.title: Ein Weltmodell des Lebens mit Alex Rives von Biohub
de.summary: In dieser Episode von The Cognitive Revolution ist Alex Rives, Head of Science bei Biohub und ehemaliger Mitbegründer von Evolutionary Scale, zu Gast. Im Mittelpunkt stehen biologische Weltmodelle, virtuelle Zellen und eine große Dateninitiative.
de.why_it_matters: Die Verbindung von künstlicher Intelligenz und Biowissenschaften bietet faszinierende Einblicke in die Zukunft der biomedizinischen Forschung und der computergestützten Biologie.
de.extended_analysis:
Die Anwendung fortschrittlicher KI-Modelle auf die Biologie eröffnet neue Wege zum Verständnis komplexer lebender Systeme. Biohub, unterstützt von der Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, verfolgt ehrgeizige wissenschaftliche Ziele im Bereich der Gesundheitsforschung.

Alex Rives teilt seine Erfahrungen aus seiner früheren Arbeit an der ESM-Modellserie von Evolutionary Scale und seiner aktuellen Rolle. Die Diskussion beleuchtet das Konzept virtueller Zellen und die Bedeutung umfangreicher Datensätze für die moderne Wissenschaft.
de.context: Der Einsatz von Machine-Learning-Techniken in der biologischen Forschung treibt den Wandel hin zu datengesteuerten Entdeckungen in der Wissenschaft voran.
key_takeaways: Einblicke von Alex Rives in biologische Weltmodelle.
Die wissenschaftlichen Ziele und Hintergründe von Biohub.
Die Bedeutung von virtuellen Zellen und datengestützter Forschung.
highlights: Gast: Alex Rives, Head of Science bei Biohub und Mitbegründer von Evolutionary Scale.
Themen: ESM-Modellserie, virtuelle Zellen und datengetriebene Biologie.

it.title: Modelli del mondo e biologia: Alex Rives spiega la spinta da 1,8 miliardi di Biohub

Vengono esplorati i requisiti di dati, le svolte nella modellazione e gli strumenti di misurazione al centro di un'iniziativa da 1,8 miliardi di dollari per sradicare le malattie.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere come i modelli computazionali avanzati possano simulare i sistemi biologici offre nuove prospettive per affrontare complesse sfide mediche e sanitarie.
it.extended_analysis:
L'episodio esamina il lavoro pionieristico svolto da Biohub per decodificare i sistemi biologici complessi attraverso modelli computazionali su larga scala. Vengono analizzati i requisiti di dati necessari per alimentare tali architetture e i recenti progressi nella misurazione.

La discussione offre uno sguardo approfondito sugli investimenti e sulle strategie impiegate per accelerare la ricerca scientifica e avvicinare la medicina a traguardi storici nella lotta alle malattie.
it.context: Il panorama della ricerca biomedica sta integrando sempre più strumenti di intelligenza artificiale e modellazione predittiva per superare i limiti dei metodi di laboratorio tradizionali.

Das Gespräch beleuchtet die wissenschaftlichen und technischen Ansätze von Biohub zur Simulation komplexer biologischer Systeme. Alex Rives erläutert die enormen Datenmengen und methodischen Durchbrüche, die für die Entwicklung virtueller Zellen erforderlich sind.
